text: Interim Town Clerk Jacqueline Wilson read the title of the Resolution. Pursuant to State law, Finance Director Robert Daddario read the TRIM statement into the record: The proposed millage rate of the Town of Cutler Bay for FY 2015-16 of 2.5348 mils per $1,000 of assessed property value within the Town of Cutler Bay is 16.01% greater than the roll-back rate of 2.1849 mils per $1,000 of assessed property value. Ad valorem taxes are being increased primarily as a result of expenditures for increased costs of contracted police services, as well as to provide for various improvements to park and public facilities. Town Manager Rafael Casals provided a brief overview and timeline of the budget process. A motion was made by Council Member Loyzelle, seconded by Vice Mayor Sochin, that this Resolution be adopted. title: RESOLUTION OF THE TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF CUTLER BAY, FLORIDA, AUTHORIZING THE TOWN MANAGER TO EXPEND FUNDS FOR THE REIMBURSEMENT OF TRAVEL COSTS FOR COMMITTEE MEMBERS; PROVIDING FOR IMPLEMENTATION; AND PROVIDING FOR AN EFFECTIVE DATE.
text: Town Clerk Debra Eastman read the title of the Resolution. Vice Mayor Loyzelle provided background information on the item. Council Member Callahan expressed concern on the approval process being decided by the committee and liaison. A motion was made by Vice Mayor Loyzelle, seconded by Council Member Mixon, that this Resolution be adopted. Council Member Mixon expressed concern that travel expenses would place committee members in the same category as a Town employee. Town Attorney Mitchell Bierman clarified it would not place them in the same category, but in an abundance of caution it would have to be discussed with risk managers if additional coverage would be needed. Mayor Bell spoke in opposition of the item. Town Manager Rafael Casals provided clarification on advice that travel authorization be made in the form of a motion as opposed to a Resolution. Vice Mayor Loyzelle spoke in favor of the item. Council Member Mixon called the question. An amended motion was made by Vice Mayor Loyzelle, seconded by Council Member Mixon that this Resolution be adopted with the change that any request be brought back to the Council for approval. Mayor Bell called for the vote and the motion failed 1-3 with Vice Mayor Loyzelle in favor and Mayor Bell, Council Member Mixon and Council Member Callahan in opposition.

title: RESOLUTION OF THE MAYOR AND TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF CUTLER BAY, FLORIDA, DESIGNATING LINCOLN CITY PARK AS A DOG PARK; PROVIDING FOR IMPLEMENTATION; AND PROVIDING FOR AN EFFECTIVE DATE.
text: Mayor Bell amended the proposed Resolution to direct the Town Manager to explore the feasibility of converting Lincoln City Park into a dog park. There was discussion on the parks master plan, and the possibility of the land being pine rockland. Mayor Bell opened Public Comments. Marty Bell spoke in favor of the Resolution. There being no one else wishing to speak, Mayor Bell closed Public Comments. There was discussion on the cost of a feasibility study and time, the possibility to look at the current site and other parks in Town for a dog park, and the possibility of extending the feasibility study to all parks, resident concerns on maintaining the park as a rockland hammock and the size of the park, the possibility of making it a passive park, and discussion in the Parks and Recreation Advisory Committee on the need for a dog park but not at this location. A motion was made by Mayor Bell, seconded by Council Member Mixon, to approve the Resolution with the amendment directing the Town Manager to look into the feasibility of Lincoln City Park becoming a future dog park. After further discussion, Mayor Bell called for the vote and the motion passed 3-2, with Council Member Coriat and Vice Mayor Loyzelle voting in opposition.

text: Town Clerk Debra Eastman read the title of the resolution. Town Attorney Chad Friedman explained the resolution, the purpose and the specifics of the lettter of intent and the opportunities and advantages to the Town. He explained that this keeps the property off the market for 120 days and the ultimate decision will be with the Town Council. Town Manager Ralph Casals explained the current assets of the Town and the current debt service. The Town Council discussed land swap details, debt service, and the process. Council Member Callahan asked about the cost of the process including the financial advisor, attorneys, etc. Vice Mayor Loyzelle made a motion to defer the resolution. There was no second offered. Council Member Callahan made a motion to cap the financial expense related to the letter of intent to $10,000. The motion received a second from Council Member Mixon. Mayor Bell called for the vote and the motion was adopted 5-0. There was further discussion regarding the cost of appraisals already done and those proposed and how that would be paid. Council Member Callahan made a motion to adopt the resolution with the amendment of the financial cap. The motion received a second from Council Member Mixon. Vice Mayor Loyzelle spoke in opposition. Mayor Bell called for a roll call vote. The motion carried by the following vote: Yes: Mayor Peggy Bell, Mary Ann Mixon, Council Member Michael Callahan and Council Member Roger Coriat 4 - No: Vice Mayor Sue Ellen Loyzelle1 -
